Two further deaths in the capital in April 2026, one of them a gay man, were linked by the attorney general's office to organised crime. An NGO observatory report counted 46 LGBT+ homicides in this state/province between 2015 and 2024, led by the capital (11), then a port city (6), two inland cities (5 each) and another city (4), with 2015 the deadliest year (10 victims).

An LGBT advocacy collective reports rising attacks in the municipalities bordering another state, that victims are no longer attended to, and that the state does not acknowledge the violence. No transfeminicide offence, no hate-crime typification, no investigative protocol - the only counterweights are individual arrests.

This state/province has no legal machinery whatsoever, plus an armed-group amplifier that makes the violence harder to escape or report.
